speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Transport if he will provide an update on whether evening ERP is still required to manage traffic congestion along the CTE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: The Land Transport Authority (LTA) will continue to monitor the situation and review the ERP charges where necessary.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I find that this is very unfair to those residents who are living in the north.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They have to pay ERP in the morning and ERP in the evening.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many residents can understand the need for having ERP in the morning.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But many feel that the evening one is not acceptable and they feel that speed is not critical when they are going home.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: While I agree with Er Dr Lee that, to some people, going home in the evening is not so critical and maybe we should not need the ERP, but I think, with the aspiration for better work-life balance, family time is important to many people nowadays.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, for the tens of thousands of motorists who are enjoying lighter traffic and higher speeds when they travel along CTE in the evening, they have been able to reach home quicker, in time for dinner and to spend quality time with their families.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, I am not sure whether they will share the same views.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Speed will affect the time required for the journeys.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: LTA's main mandate is to ensure that motorists are able to enjoy smooth and safe journeys on the roads and expressways.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Without the ERP, all motorists on the north-bound CTE are more likely to experience jams in the evening.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is expected, as our northern areas are more densely populated, which includes Nee Soon South, where the Member's constituency is.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But with ERP, it alleviates this traffic congestion.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We have data to show that, with ERP or when ERP rates are adjusted accordingly, it does shape motorists' behaviour and it alleviates the situation and, at the same time, provides options for commuters.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, those who are willing to pay the ERP charges can enjoy a shorter journey home while others can choose other routes.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, going up north, they can choose Thomson Road which is not a priced road, or they can take public transport.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In addition, my Ministry has been working very hard to improve these other options.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For example, we are constructing the North-South Corridor and the MRT resignalling works will help to increase train frequencies.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So, even though we live in a very densely populated city, it is our commitment to provide Singaporeans with a quality living environment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Precisely because of work-life balance, a lot of my residents say "Why not we just get rid of the evening ERP?" because many of them stay longer in the office and go home only after ERP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: So, I would like to urge the Minister to seriously reconsider because the fact that the speed along the CTE did not change much over these few years says that it is no longer effective.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But we note Er Dr Lee's concern for her constituents and I think, in general, Singaporeans' family time, and we will continue to look at ways to manage our traffic conditions better.
